holidays.name: National Sticky Bun Day
holidays.description: A gooey, cinnamon-drenched celebration of the swirled pastry dripping with caramel, pecans, and pure joy. Bakers and breakfast fans unite to peel, pull, and lick their fingers clean.
holidays.origin: Sticky buns are commonly linked to German immigrants in Pennsylvania, the Pennsylvania Dutch, who brought their schnecken pastries to America in the 1700s. The food day itself is an unofficial observance spread by food bloggers and baking enthusiasts.
holidays.funFact: Sticky buns are sometimes called 'schnecken,' which is German for 'snails,' because of their spiral shape.

holidays.name: International Mother Language Day
holidays.description: A global observance celebrating linguistic diversity, the languages we grow up speaking, and the importance of keeping endangered tongues alive. Perfect for bragging about your grandma's slang.
holidays.origin: UNESCO proclaimed it in 1999, and it has been observed worldwide since 2000. The date honors students killed in 1952 in Dhaka, Bangladesh, while protesting for recognition of the Bengali language.
holidays.funFact: Roughly 40 percent of the world's approximately 7,000 languages are considered endangered, and one language disappears about every two weeks.

holidays.name: National Card Reading Day
holidays.description: A day for sitting down and actually rereading the greeting cards you've saved in a shoebox, drawer, or under a pile of old mail. Expect nostalgia, mild crying, and questionable birthday puns.
holidays.origin: The observance appears to have been created by greeting card enthusiasts to encourage people to revisit and treasure meaningful messages from loved ones.
holidays.funFact: Americans buy around 6.5 billion greeting cards each year, so there is a lot of reading material out there.

holidays.name: National Grain-Free Day
holidays.description: A day for skipping wheat, rice, and oats, and for exploring recipes built on nuts, veggies, and creative flour substitutes. Bread lovers may observe it with great suffering.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food-and-wellness observance that grew from the popularity of paleo, keto, and gluten-free eating trends in recent years.
holidays.funFact: Humans have been farming grains for roughly 10,000 years, so going grain-free takes you back to the pre-agricultural menu.

holidays.name: Love Your Pet Day
holidays.description: A day when pet owners are officially encouraged to spoil their furry, scaly, or feathery roommates with treats, cuddles, and an obscene number of photos.
holidays.origin: An unofficial pet-themed observance popularized by pet lovers and animal-focused websites, held in the cozy days after Valentine's Day so the love can extend to non-human companions.
holidays.funFact: Surveys regularly show that over 60 percent of pet owners consider their pets full members of the family, and many include them in holiday cards.
